title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
By July 2023, selected Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), including informal associations and cooperatives in selected sub-sectors were capacitated to upgrade their membership services and equipped with new business and e-commerce skills development program through partnerships with Business Development Fund (BDF); Business Development service provider and value chain actor, and Private Sector Foundation [PSF], to establish niche markets relevant to Rwandan tailor-made products With the support from Multi Partner Trust Fund (One UN fund); RWA/22/01/OUF, ILO entered, in April 2023, into partnership agreement with the Private Sector Foundation [PSF] to design and deliver new business and e-commerce skills development programs to MSMEs for them to develop strategies to market Rwandan made products.
In the context of the PSF mission to promote business resilience and SME development, 30 tailors’ representatives of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) were equipped in July 2023 with new business and e-commerce skills through ILO-PSF partnership to establish niche markets relevant to Rwandan tailor-made products. Moreover, they were trained on value addition in textile to become more competitive in the market.
Another agreement was negotiated in July 2023 with Business Development Fund (BDF) to build the capacity of informal sector associations and cooperatives in selected sub-sectors to better serve their women and men members and improve access to financial products

Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative: From April 2022, Rwanda Ministry of Ministry of Public Service and Labour (MIFOTRA) operationalized an institutional capacity development programme for her inter-ministerial secretariat on the National Employment Policy (NEP) for it to provide effective co-ordination, monitoring and evaluation of the revised NEP 2019, including monitoring of employment mainstreaming in districts plans and sector ministries With the support from Multi Partner Trust Fund (One UN fund); RWA/22/01/OUF, ILO extended technical support to the NEP co-ordination secretariat that included technical training workshops for members of the NEP secretariat [on co-ordination mechanism for NEP]. The Office further supported and faciliated NEP secretariat field monitoring visits in selected districts to assess mainstreaming of employment in Districts’ plans. By the way of same resources, ILO further facilitated in April 2022, workshop for enhancing coordination of employment mainstreaming & workplace learning initiatives at district level convened by the MIFOTRA. The workshop targeted district staff in charge of education, business development and employment promotion. The workshop participants were familiarized with different strategies that can be reinforced in order to effectively and efficiently coordinate skills development and employment promotion interventions at district level. In the aftermath of the workshop, the employment ecosystem at districts level is fully operational
